12: ובמוקדשין And regarding consecrated [animals] - Ab initio, [one who is impure] may not slaughter, even with a long knife, since he is warned from the Torah that he must not cause [a sacrifice] to become impure, as it is written (Num. 18:8), "Behold I have given over to you the guarding of my terumah-gifts[, and all the consecrated things of the Children of Israel, etc.]." Wherefore, in regards to the of "guarding," our Rabbis decreed that [an impure person may not slaughter] ab initio on account of [the maxim], "Go, go, we say to a Nazirite. Go around, go around, [but] do not come near to the vineyard" (Avodah Zarah 17a:6).

שחיטתן כשרה His slaughter is valid - For we had [to account for] the after-the-fact [language] from the Mishna. And below it explains how it can be [that an impure] person does not defile the knife, and then goes back and defiles the meat itself (i.e., through the knife) (see Hul. 3a:1-2).
